items.title: The scaled three-torus as a smooth compact flat spatial manifold
items.design_state: New local prerequisite authored on the A page because no current carrier supplied the exact smooth scaled-torus geometry used by the assigned B example.
items.statement:
Let $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ be real periods, let
$\Lambda:=L_1\mathbb Z\times L_2\mathbb Z\times L_3\mathbb Z\subseteq\mathbb R^3$,
and let $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_L:=\mathbb R^3/\Lambda$ be the quotient
map with the quotient topology. Then $q$ is a smooth local diffeomorphism and
$\mathbb T^3_L$ is a compact,
Hausdorff, second-countable smooth three-manifold without boundary.

The forms $dx^1,dx^2,dx^3$ and coordinate vector fields
$\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ on $\mathbb R^3$ descend to global smooth
forms and vector fields on $\mathbb T^3_L$. Every smooth $\Lambda$-periodic
function on $\mathbb R^3$ descends to a smooth function on $\mathbb T^3_L$.
Consequently, $M_L:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\mathbb T^3_L$ has a smooth,
boundaryless four-manifold structure and carries the smooth Lorentzian metric,
orientation, and time orientation

$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_0,\qquad o:=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3.$$

In the product charts from the quotient atlas the metric has constant matrix
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and its metric-selected Christoffel symbols
vanish.

references.title: Klaus Wirthmüller, Manifolds (lecture notes 2011–2016), §1.14(4), printed pp. 12–13 (PDF pp. 18–19)
references.locator: The quotient group R^n/Z^n; small cube quotient charts, local translation transition maps, the smooth atlas, and the quotient map as a local diffeomorphism. The current item proves the scaled-period, product-space, descended-field, and metric details directly.

items.title: Sourced Maxwell sign and current conservation
items.design_state: Complete conditional mathematical proof authored; all inspected current suppliers are published and present.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

items.title: Compact potential and metric variation of the Maxwell action
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof authored; actual batch-2 connection-data carriers match the used interface, but their seven inherited prerequisites remain unavailable; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and let $c,\mu_0>0$ be fixed
real coefficients. The action density is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If a differentiable source-sector functional on the same variations satisfies
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

**(b) Metric variation.** For a smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse
metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, section 3.2.5 and section 4.5.3
references.locator: Section 3.2.5, equations (3.114)–(3.115), Maxwell action, source variation and charge flux; §4.5.3, metric variation of the Maxwell action and its stress tensor.

items.title: Gauss charge and finite-chain flux balance
items.design_state: Complete finite-chain proof authored from the current-form result and inspected Stokes/flux suppliers.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TM)$ be smooth, and fix constants
$c,\mu_0>0$. Assume
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, equivalently
$d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. A finite smooth singular $k$-chain means
a finite formal real linear combination of smooth singular $k$-simplices,
with the boundary operation of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]].

For a finite smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$, define its charge by

$$Q(\Sigma):=\frac1c\int_\Sigma\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then:

**(a) Gauss charge formula.** For every such $\Sigma$,

$$Q(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_{\partial\Sigma}\star_gF.$$

Consequently, if $\partial\Sigma=0$, then $Q(\Sigma)=0$. This is the
compact-cycle neutrality constraint for a smooth everywhere-defined sourced
field.

**(b) Bounding-surface restriction.** For every finite smooth singular
three-chain $V$, the magnetic flux through its boundary vanishes:

$$\int_{\partial V}F=0.$$

The equation $dF=0$ does not imply that the flux through every closed
two-cycle is zero; this item gives a zero-flux conclusion only when the cycle
is the boundary of a finite smooth chain in the field domain. Likewise, the
electric flux formula in (a) identifies charge with flux only for a bounding
surface.

**(c) Charge balance.** If a finite smooth singular four-chain $C$ satisfies
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for three-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$Q(\Sigma_2)-Q(\Sigma_1)=-Q(B).$$

Equal charge on the two slices therefore requires zero net side flux. No
asymptotic charge or flux at infinity is asserted; noncompact limits require
separate convergence and boundary-flux hypotheses.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, section 3.2.5
references.locator: Section 3.2.5, electric charge, the sourced form equation, Stokes flux formula (3.115), and charge change through a timelike side boundary.

items.title: Maxwell stress tensor in an observer frame
items.design_state: Complete conditional component proof authored; the variational tensor supplier remains conditional on the escalated batch-2 chain and its seven missing inherited inputs.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$
be open, let $n$ be a smooth observer congruence on $U$, and let $F$ be a
smooth real two-form. Fix $c,\mu_0>0$ and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Assume the fixed-sector variational hypotheses
and tensor formula supplied conditionally by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], namely

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}:=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

For the smooth observer covectors $E,B$ of
[[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], define the rest projector
$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a_b+n^an_b$ and the observer energy flux
$S_n^a:=-c\,h^a{}_bT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{bc}n_c$. Then:

**(a) Tensor symmetries.** $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ is symmetric and
$g^{ab}T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=0$.

**(b) Orthonormal observer components.** In any positively oriented
orthonormal tetrad with $E_0=n$ and spatial orientation
$\epsilon_{123}=+1$, the components are

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{00}=\frac12\left(\epsilon_0\sum_iE_i^2+\frac1{\mu_0}\sum_iB_i^2\right),\qquad T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{0i}=\frac{(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)_i}{\mu_0c},$$

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ij}=-\left[\epsilon_0\left(E_iE_j-\frac12\delta_{ij}\sum_kE_k^2\right)+\frac1{\mu_0}\left(B_iB_j-\frac12\delta_{ij}\sum_kB_k^2\right)\right].$$

Here $(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)_i:=\epsilon_{ijk}E_jB_k$. In particular,
$T_{\mathrm{EM},0i}=-T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{0i}$ in this tetrad.

**(c) Observer energy and flux.** The measured energy density
$u_n:=T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}n^an^b$ equals the nonnegative value in part (b), and
the spatial vector $S_n$ has components
$S_n^i=(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)_i/\mu_0$ and $S_n^0=0$.

**(d) Geometric normalization.** For every smooth real two-form $H$, define

$$Q_g(H)_{ab}:=H_{ac}H_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}H_{cd}H^{cd}.$$

For every real constant $\lambda$, $Q_g(\lambda H)=\lambda^2Q_g(H)$. Fix also a formal constant $G_N>0$, and use the positive square-root convention of [[def-emg-explicit-power-regimes]] to set

$$\alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad\mathcal F:=\alpha F,\qquad\kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$

Then $\alpha>0$ and

$$\kappa_ET_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=2Q_g(\mathcal F)_{ab}.$$

For formal SI dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates $x^0=ct$, take dimensionless $g_{ab}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}\,A^{-2}}$, and $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$. Then $[T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{m^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$, $[\mathcal F_{ab}]=\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and both sides of the last identity have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. Components in angular or other scaled coordinates acquire their units through the coordinate Jacobian. A two-form $\mathcal F$ integrated over an oriented two-surface has length units under these assignments. These conventions introduce no measured constant or physical field-law premise.

These are conditional mathematical tensor identities. The batch-2 connection carriers are authored drafts. No independent proof acceptance or native readiness is claimed here.
